advisories.title: Make the administrator-capability test match its claim
advisories.body: The test says it grants every declared capability but exercises only `staff:manage`. Rename it to the capability it covers, or iterate the declared capability list, so a future capability cannot be mistakenly assumed covered.
evidence: Premise: __tests__/authorization.test.ts:84 names every declared capability, while line 92 invokes requireCapability only for staff:manage → Improvement: keeps the test name and its actual contract aligned → Fix: either rename the case or assert each Capability value.
lib/auth/authorization.ts:8-20 → Capability is a finite explicit union, so an exhaustive table-driven test is bounded.

advisories.title: Do not label the absent-user case as an Administrator guard
advisories.body: This setup makes `findFirst` return undefined, so both actions exit through their missing-user branch. The test name claims it protects an Administrator, which can mislead a future maintainer about what regression it catches. Rename the case to the missing/non-secretariat target behavior, or add a fake-DB predicate assertion that proves the secretaria role filter.
evidence: Premise: __tests__/staff-and-observations.test.ts:27 calls the scenario an Administrator case, but line 28 configures findFirst to return undefined → Improvement: makes the regression suite's stated protection truthful → Fix: rename it or assert the role-constrained lookup.
app/admin/_actions/staff-actions.ts:44-51 and 61-68 → production protection is the secretaria-constrained query, not an Administrator object returned by this test double.

advisories.title: Represent secretariat loading results with exported types instead of casts
advisories.body: The card casts both server-action results to local state types. Those casts conceal any contract drift in the operational projection, including relation nullability or a future document-field change. Export the small view-model types from the action/module (or derive state from Awaited<ReturnType<...>>) and type state to them so TypeScript checks the boundary.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:103-109 declares local anonymous state shapes and force-casts both Promise results → Improvement: type-checks the server-to-client operational projection rather than trusting it → Fix: export/reuse concrete observation and issued-document view-model types.
app/admin/_actions/observation-actions.ts:8-15 and app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:794-808 → both action return shapes are available at the boundary and can be named once.

advisories.title: Give secretariat async operations an explicit error state
advisories.body: Loading, note submission, and document download discard rejected promises or `{ error }` results. A failed request therefore leaves the card unchanged with no explanation and makes retry behavior implicit. Centralize these calls behind a loading/error state and render the returned message, preserving the existing successful path.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:107-110 attaches only a then handler, while lines 112-123 ignore unsuccessful action results → Improvement: makes operational failures visible and retryable instead of silent → Fix: catch request failures and store/render an error state for loading, saving, and downloading.
app/admin/_actions/observation-actions.ts:22-36 and app/admin/_actions/admin-actions.ts:810-821 → these actions deliberately return error variants that the component currently does not surface.

advisories.title: Expand the new role-specific JSX before it grows further
advisories.body: The added role-specific components keep most state transitions and nested markup on single physical lines. This makes access-control changes, DOM structure, and future error-state additions much harder to review than the surrounding project style. Reformat the components into named handlers and multiline JSX; no behavior change is required.
evidence: Premise: app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:100-136 contains the card's state, effects, handlers, and nested controls in a compact block unlike the established multiline component style below line 141 → Improvement: lowers review and modification cost for role-specific UI → Fix: expand the component and extract its repeated view fragments into readable JSX.
app/admin/benfeitores/client.tsx:93-101 and app/admin/_components/issued-documents.tsx:8-13 → the same compact style was introduced in the other new role/document views.

suppressions.candidate: Rename the local Document type because it shadows the DOM global
suppressions.note: The component does not use the DOM Document global, so the shadowing has no concrete local cost beyond preference.
